Tests green (2/2), `BUILD SUCCESS`. Here's how I addressed each finding.

**1. Duplicated postcode normalization — fixed.** Extracted `Household.normalizePostcode(String)` as the single definition, routed `Household.key` through it, and replaced `FlagPossibleDuplicate`'s inline `normalize(...)` (now deleted) with calls to it. Soft-match and household membership now share one postcode-normalization rule.

**2. SHA-256-hex implemented twice (three times, actually) — fixed.** Added `model.Sha256.hex(String)` as the single digest-to-lowercase-hex routine (with the one `NoSuchAlgorithmException → IllegalStateException` handler). Callers now take what they need from it:
- `Owner.identityKey` → full 64-hex (removed `Owner.sha256Hex` and its now-unused imports).
- `Household.id` → `"H-" + Sha256.hex(...).substring(0, 12)`.
- `AssignCustomerCode.hash8` → `Sha256.hex(...).substring(0, 8).toUpperCase(...)` — not flagged, but it was a third copy of the same pattern, so folding it in keeps "one place this lives" honest. All three produce byte-identical outputs to before (customer codes, household ids, identity keys unchanged).

I put `Sha256` in the `model` package (alongside the existing `TelephoneFormatter` utility) rather than `util`, because `util` already depends on `model` (`EntityUtils → BaseEntity`); placing it in `util` would have created a `model`↔`util` package cycle, whereas `model` keeps the dependency one-directional.

**Minor (soundex on `Owner`) — left as-is, with reasoning.** The reviewer flagged this as non-blocking and defensible. There's no existing text/normalization util (the `util` package holds only `EntityUtils`, an entity lookup), and `soundex` exists solely to feed `Owner.identityKey`, which also lives on `Owner`. Moving just `soundex` out while `identityKey` stays would split one cohesive derivation across two classes for no real gain, so I left it co-located with its only caller.

No acceptance behaviour changed — all derived values are computed identically; this was a pure structural de-duplication.
